source: វិទ្យាការទប់ស្កាត់ និងកម្ចាត់សមាសភាពបទព្រុងលើដំណាំទុរេន (Prevention and Control of Harmful Organisms on Durian), Cambodian technical extension document compiled with reference to CABI Crop Protection Compendium and durian pest/disease literature, 28pp
text: African red mite (Eutetranychus africanus) is a tiny mite pest that feeds on the underside of durian leaves, causing a stippled, bronzed, or dulled appearance on the leaf surface where large numbers are present; heavy, sustained infestation can reduce the leaf's ability to photosynthesize and stress the tree. Mite populations tend to build up faster in hot, dry conditions with low humidity and can be knocked back by heavy rain or overhead irrigation, which physically dislodges them from the leaf surface. General control approach: monitor the underside of leaves regularly, especially during dry-season stretches, and treat with a miticide when populations are building, following label guidance; growers should be cautious about broad-spectrum insecticide overuse against other pests, since killing off the mites' natural predators (predatory mites and other beneficial insects) can sometimes make mite outbreaks worse rather than better.
